page.layout: Running head at top: "Animalium Mar. Ordo XII." with page number 180 at top left. Below the running head, a line of text at full width (continuation of previous page). Then a woodcut of a boar-like sea creature (Wodiser Walfisch) at full width, followed by a German caption below it at full width. Then a second woodcut of a monstrous sea creature (Cetus barbatus), followed by a main text block of the Latin paragraph at full width, with a marginal note at the left margin ("Scolopendra marina.") beside it. Below the text, a German heading line "GERMAN. F. Ein Bartwal." at full width. Signature-like word "CETVM" at the bottom right corner.

main_text.l: quam Apri fuit, corium munitum ueluti conchis pectinum.
GERM. Wodiser Walfisch nit ein Herill ist/von den Teutschen in Seeland vnnd
anderschwo genannt/so mag er genamset werden ein Wal_åber/oder ein Schweynwal. Der
nam Schweynwal sol sunst gebraucht werden vonn einem Walfisch/der auff xxx. Klaffter
MONSTRVM hoc(inquit Olaus) maximum est, & cornibus, & uisu flammeo horrendum.
Oculi circunferentia sedecim uel uiginti pedum mensuram continet. Caput (quadratum,
Cardanus) in quatuor mucrones diuiditur. Barba prolixa est. Pars posterior parua existimatur.
Nos Cetum barbatum appellauimus, &c. Quatuordecim cornibus radiatum caput apparet, cor-
nua utrinq; ab oculo incipiunt, & per occipitium transeunt: nescio quàm recte. Albertus enim ce-
tis nostrorum marium appendices quasdam esse scribit (circa oculos) ciliorum instar, corneas, o-
cto ferè pedes longas, plus minùs, pro magnitudine beluæ, specie magnæ falcis fœnisecum, ducen-
tas & quinquaginta super oculum unum, & totidem super alterum, ex lato in acutum desinentes,
non rigidas, sed iacentes, & dispositas uersus tempora, ita ut ueluti os unum latum magni uanni
instar efficiant, quo belua aduersus tempestates oculos muniens operiat. Oculi unius foueam
homines quindecim, aliquando uiginti capere. ¶ De hoc Ceto sentit Rondeletius, ubi picturas
Tabulæ Olai reprehendens, scribit, Scolopendram cetaceam monstrosam ab eo pictam esse, qua-
drato capite, promissa barba. Mihi hac ratione non recte à Rondeletio reprehendi uidetur, &c.

page.notes: Woodcut of a boar-like fish with scales, tusks and tail, above the German caption; woodcut of a monstrous sea creature with horns and barbels, above the Latin text. The German caption at the top is set in mixed roman and black letter type; "Walfisch" and "Herill" are read as printed. The marginal note "Scolopendra marina." is in italic at left. The "CETVM" word at lower right is treated as a catchword.
